beats.care: Expect hype in your group chats. Strong big-fund demand does not guarantee a profitable listing, and IPO money can be lost.
beats.what: Global and Indian funds bid around ₹2.5 lakh crore for Jio's ₹8,110 crore anchor portion, reports say, before the public offer opens tomorrow.
beats.why: Jio is raising ₹30,213 crore at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 a share, which values it near $108 billion at the top price.

cards.body: Reported anchor bidders include BlackRock, Fidelity, Singapore's GIC, Norway's sovereign fund, LIC and several Indian mutual funds. Up to ₹27,500 crore of the money raised is meant to repay Reliance Jio Infocomm's loans.
Anchors are large institutions that commit early. Their demand signals confidence and helps set the mood, but they buy at the same price band and can also be wrong.
cards.title: why do ipos have anchor investors?

cards.body: Jio says it carries about 60% of all mobile data traffic in India, with a projected 53 crore subscribers as of June 2026.

cards.q: Does hype make you want to invest?

opts: Big funds are keen, but listing gains aren't certain
cards.q: What does huge anchor demand tell you?
cards.why: Anchor demand shows interest from big funds, but no one can promise how the share will trade after listing.

cover.label: anchor demand vs shares on offer

hook: Big funds wanted *30x more* Jio shares than were on offer. Why?

learn.t: An anchor book is an IPO slice sold to big funds before the public. Jio's drew bids over 30 times its size.

watch: Public bidding runs 21–23 Oct. Spill's prediction on whether the public part gets fully subscribed closes on 23 Oct.
